RUSTED BLOOM GREENHOUSE — long-neglected Victorian greenhouse with rust-patinaed iron framework, aged glass panes clouded with humidity, bloom-mass having consumed most visible architecture, wisteria and climbing rose overtaking the ridge, wild atmospheric density pressing against every surface.

SMALL CURVED-ROOF PRIVATE HOUSE — small single-room estate-house Victorian conservatory with curved glass roof, iron glazing-bar ribs, trailing fuchsia and passionflower consuming the interior, central stone bench buried beneath bloom-cascade, diffuse soft light filtering through the vine-covered glass overhead.

KEW SCALE IRON DOME — Kew-Gardens-lineage palm-house with soaring multi-tier glass dome, iron columns in rust-patina rising to the crown, central avenue beneath towering palm canopy, tree-ferns arching overhead, climbing glory-vine and philodendron consuming every column base upward.

VICTORIAN ROUND ROTUNDA — circular iron-and-glass rotunda with peripheral column arcade, central stone pedestal beneath the dome peak, climbing clematis and roses threading each column, glass-dome above dividing honeyed afternoon light into column-shadows across the mossy tile floor.

CONSERVATORY WING PROMENADE — long Victorian conservatory wing with barrel-vaulted iron-and-glass ceiling, iron column arcade along one side, central bloom-avenue receding in depth, climbing rose and wisteria consuming the upper vault, humid warm luminescence filling the receding interior distance.

LAEKEN WINTER GARDEN — vast Crystal-Palace-scale rotunda with soaring rust-patina iron ribs converging at a central oculus, cathedral-volume interior drowning in cascading wisteria and trumpet-vine, multiple bloom-tiers rising toward the iron-framed dome far above.

COUNTRY-HOUSE LEAN-TO CONSERVATORY — single-room lean-to estate conservatory built against warm south-facing brick, sloped Victorian glazing overhead, wrought-iron staging heavy with pelargonium cascades, espaliered climbing roses consuming the rear wall in a dense fragrant mass.

KEW PALM HOUSE INTERIOR — vast multi-tier glass dome soaring on rust-patina iron columns, central avenue between towering Washingtonia palms and tree-ferns, bloom-beds bordering every walkway, humid golden light filtering through iron-ribbed glass panels far overhead.

OCTAGONAL FINIAL CONSERVATORY — eight-sided Victorian conservatory with leaded-glass panels converging at an ornate iron finial peak, central stone sundial surrounded by climbing passionflower, each of the eight glass bays overgrown with a different cascading bloom species.

SCHÖNBRUNN HOTHOUSE NAVE — botanical-garden hothouse with steeply-pitched glass roof, multi-aisle nave of wrought-iron walkways receding in crisp sharp overlapping layers, bloom-beds flanking every aisle, banana-fronds and tree-ferns arching high across the central nave in dense tropical canopy.

GLASS-DOME TOWER ROTUNDA — tower-shaped conservatory with circular base and conical iron-ribbed peak, spiral wrought-iron staircase ascending through a central column of climbing clematis, glass panels clear and bright, fern-fronds pressing against every pane from within.

VICTORIAN ORANGERY FORMAL — tall arched iron-and-glass windows along three walls, geometric slate-tile floor reflecting amber light, formal arrangement of citrus standards in terracotta urns, iron-framed ceiling draped with trailing jasmine, the atmosphere thick with warm perfumed air.

CRYSTAL-PALACE EXHIBITION NAVE — cathedral-volume Crystal-Palace-scale interior with multiple floors of iron-framed galleries, soaring transept of glass overhead, climbing bloom-masses consuming every iron column from base to capital, the vast interior filled with diffused white light through hundreds of panes.

HALF-DOME ATTACHED OBSERVATORY — half-dome glass-and-iron lean-to pressed against a dressed-stone country-mansion wall, curved iron ribs arching from the wall-plate to the ridge, the curved glass dominating the upper register, interior dense with climbing hydrangea and maiden-hair fern.

GLASS-CORRIDOR PROMENADE — long Victorian glass-corridor with iron-arched ceiling connecting two brick wings, climbing-bloom cascades descending from every iron rib, depth receding in crisp sharp overlapping layers toward the far end in warm golden light, the tiled floor dark with moisture and fallen petals.

ROTUNDA GLASS-HOUSE POOL — circular rotunda glass-house, central reflecting pool edged by moss-covered stone, wrought-iron peripheral walkway encircling the interior, glass dome ribbed in intricate Victorian ironwork above, climbing roses and passionflower consuming every column between walkway and dome.

VICTORIAN PEACH-HOUSE — wall-attached Victorian peach-house with steeply-sloped single-span glass roof, espaliered climbing bloom trained across the entire rear brick wall in tight geometric fans, central narrow aisle between low wrought-iron staging, sun-warmed atmosphere heavy with sweet floral fragrance.

BUTTERFLY GLASS-HOUSE — Victorian butterfly-house with low tropical glass-dome of intricate iron lattice, central mossy pool ringed by cascading climbing-bloom, clear interior air, fern-fronds and hibiscus pressing against the lower glass panes in a dense tangled mass.

LAEKEN ANNEX PALM PAVILION — medium-scale palm-pavilion with multi-tier iron-ribbed glass dome, rust-patina columns lining a central avenue between dense tropical planting, towering Kentia palms reaching toward the upper glass tier, bloom-cascades descending from every iron capital in heavy fragrant curtains.

VICTORIAN ALPINE HOUSE — low-profile Victorian alpine glasshouse with shallow-pitch iron-ribbed glass roof close overhead, interior dense with climbing alpines and cascading auricula on wrought-iron tiered staging, the glass panes jewelled with condensation, a narrow central path between the massed bloom-beds.

CONSERVATORY BARREL-VAULT NAVE — barrel-vault Victorian conservatory with continuous iron-and-glass ceiling arching overhead in a single graceful curve, long central nave flanked by bloom-beds on raised iron staging, climbing jasmine consuming the curved iron ribs, warm amber light filtering the length of the nave.

OCTAGONAL PALM ROTUNDA — octagonal glass-and-iron rotunda conservatory scaled to a public botanic garden, eight tall bays of leaded glass between slender iron columns, central avenue of potted palms rising toward the eight-sided iron dome above, climbing bloom-masses filling every bay with dense cascading growth.
